purpose: Additive native-resolution camera development retrieval; separate from frozen historical and held-out sets. Runtime claims require the dated source-specific ledger.

questions.query: Why did a magnified camera pan jump whole simulation cells, and how does native display-pixel scrolling keep the pixel world sharp?
facts: Main floored the camera before the shader, and the palette fragment separately floored view coordinates before adding that origin.
The candidate keeps continuous camera state, snaps the complete final screen translation, then floors the combined world sample and nearest-samples the cell centre.
The native cell physics and simulation resolution are unchanged.

questions.query: How do painting, selection, clipboard and agent focus pick the correct cell at a fractional camera position and fractional zoom?
facts: Picking maps the pointer physical pixel centre through the displayed transform and floors the complete world coordinate.
The displayed origin is shared by PAINT previews, selection, overlays and Art focus; agent image metadata describes the actual rounded crop with fractional world bounds.
Native mutations remain integer cell coordinates.

questions.query: Does cursor-centred wheel zoom accumulate rounding drift after repeatedly zooming in and out?
facts: Zoom solves a continuous world anchor and never writes the snapped presentation origin into camera state.
Away from clamped bounds the two rounding phases can produce at most one physical pixel per axis of visible anchor difference; there is no accumulating camera-state error.
World-edge clamping can intentionally prevent exact anchor preservation.

questions.query: How much glow and vapour guard space covers fractional camera scrolling without a full-resolution effect buffer?
facts: Glow is fixed at two world cells per source texel and uses five guard texels on each side plus one far-edge texel.
Vapour ping-pong history buffers use W+1 by H+1 integer-world texels and resize together.
The final composite reprojects those small buffers to the displayed camera; native capacity is unchanged.

questions.query: How do I launch and accept the native-resolution pixel scrolling Windows evaluation, and can headless tests authorize its merge?
facts: Use the camera-labelled qualified artifact, extract it completely and run Open Workbench.cmd.
At 2x or greater magnification slowly middle-drag, test stationary edges, cursor zoom, editing, Undo/Redo, Art focus, following, resizing and physical Windows display scale.
Headless parsing does not qualify graphical motion, physical Windows scaling or human feel; the candidate remains Draft until owner acceptance.
